title: Strayhorn joining the band and writing for Johnny Hodges
summary: Strayhorn was respected once they played his music; his only band number was A Train, the rest written with and for Hodges.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Right. Well, that's very good. Well, Cootie, remember back, I mean, the guys must have thought it was an amazing thing for a little guy like Sweet Pea to show up in the bus and everything. Didn't they?
No.
Why not?
They didn't pay nobody no mind. They had to do their thing.
Well, I guess as soon as they knew what
he'd written and everything, when they heard -- when they sat down and played the music he'd written, well then they knew what kind of musician he was.
Oh, well, yeah. Yeah. They had a lot of respect for him. They knew. They knew who he was.
Because he was a number of years younger than most everybody else in the band --
Yeah.
-- wasn't he?
Uh-huh.
And then another thing, he had a different kind of a background, too, because he'd gone through college. Didn't he have a degree in music and all that kind of thing?
Well, I don't know his history.
No.
I don't know.
No. But --
The only thing that he ever did write, other than with Johnny, was the "A Train".
Yeah. Yeah. That's right. That's the only band number he did, really, wasn't it?
Yeah. All the other things he did was with Johnny Hodges.
Yeah. Yeah. Well, that was his way. That was his thing. I mean, like "Lush Life" was his number, and
that was it, wasn't it?
All the beautiful things. All the pretty things. He wrote those with Johnny.

Yeah. Although, Cootie, I'll tell you, he did a band number that I thought was one of the most beautiful things I ever heard, which you were in the band, I'm quite sure. Do you remember "Blood Count"?
That was Johnny Hodges.
Yeah, it was written for Johnny. That's quite true, it was.
Everything he did was for Johnny Hodges.
Yeah. Yeah.
The Beautiful things.
Yeah.
That was about one of the last things he did.
He sent that down from hospital, yeah.
Yes.

Yeah. It's a gorgeous thing. Beautiful thing. Yeah, that's perfectly true. That's really right. I guess that isn't really recognized the same way. Other than "A Train". And "A Train" was one of the first ones he wrote, wasn't it?
Yeah.
For the band. But, you know --
I wasn't there. I had left.
Oh, you had.
Yeah.
